text:
tim_customer: Hey team — after we flipped routing to the shared-network TGW, some of our services in private-subnet-c are getting intermittent 502s and TLS errors calling Redwood. Only affects that subnet, other subnets fine. Any quick checks?

alice_support: sorry about that @tim_customer. Can you paste a representative error and confirm whether it's a TCP timeout, TLS cert mismatch, or an HTTP 502 from an intermediate?

tim_customer: We see both. Example from service logs: 
```
2026-03-14T22:11:08Z ERROR http: upstream 502 bad gateway
2026-03-14T22:11:09Z ERROR dial tcp 52.24.130.10:443: i/o timeout
2026-03-14T22:11:09Z ERROR tls: handshake error: remote error: tls: bad certificate (server cert CN=*.elb.amazonaws.com)
```

raj_engineer: Quick checks — is the Redwood endpoint an interface endpoint (PrivateLink) in your VPC? Did you enable the private DNS option when creating the endpoint? And are you using the central Route53 resolver via TGW?

tim_customer: Yes VPCE (vpce-0c9f) with private DNS enabled. We moved DNS to central-dns via TGW resolver endpoints during the migration.

maya_network: Sounds like a split-horizon/resolution path. From an instance in private-subnet-c run `dig +short api.redwood.team` and `curl -v https://api.redwood.team/health` and paste outputs. Also check `getent hosts api.redwood.team`.

tim_customer: Ran those on a repro host: 
```
$ dig +short api.redwood.team
34.200.130.10

$ curl -v https://api.redwood.team/health
* Connected to 34.200.130.10 (34.200.130.10) port 443
* TLS handshake: server certificate: subject CN=*.elb.amazonaws.com
* SSL: certificate subject name '*.elb.amazonaws.com' does not match 'api.redwood.team'
* Closing connection 0
```
From private-subnet-a (pre-migration) the dig returns `10.5.22.9`.

alice_support: That confirms DNS resolving to the public ELB for hosts using the central resolver path. If DNS returns a public IP you'll hit the public ELB which presents the ELB cert (SNI mismatch) or be routed through NAT and hit timeouts.

raj_engineer: Did you attach the private hosted zone (PHZ) that maps `api.redwood.team` to the vpce name to the central-dns VPC? If central resolver VPC doesn't have the PHZ association, queries forwarded from TGW will fall back to public DNS.

tim_customer: I checked — PHZ is associated only to service-vpc (the old VPC), not to central-dns. We assumed TGW resolver would inherit it.

maya_network: TGW doesn't magically attach PHZs — you need either: 1) attach the PHZ to the resolver VPC (central-dns), or 2) create a Route53 Resolver outbound rule in central-dns that forwards the zone to the VPC owning the PHZ via resolver endpoints.

infra_bot: checklist: `aws route53 list-hosted-zones-by-vpc --vpc-id vpc-central`, `aws route53resolver list-resolver-rule-associations --filters Name=VPC,Values=vpc-central`.

raj_engineer: Also watch for cached answers on instances/services — systemd-resolved and dnsmasq can keep the public answer until TTL expires. Use `sudo systemd-resolve --flush-caches` or restart dnsmasq.

tim_customer: We associated the PHZ with central-dns and flushed caches. `dig +short api.redwood.team` now returns `10.5.22.9` from private-subnet-c.

alice_support: Good. After association, did you still see timeouts or resets? If so check security groups / NACLs — if your egress only allows TCP:443 and blocks ephemeral, return path may be blocked causing connect/timeouts.

tim_customer: We had SG egress locked to 443 only. We opened ephemeral ports 1024-65535 outbound and re-tested. Timeouts disappeared.

raj_engineer: One more subtlety: if central-dns forwards unknown zones to the internet (eg an outbound rule to 8.8.8.8 or an outbound resolver endpoint that doesn't know the PHZ), queries can leak externally. Ensure central-dns has a resolver rule for `api.redwood.team` that either forwards to the VPC with the PHZ or resolves locally.

maya_network: Repro steps we ran for customers in similar cases: 
```
# from repro host
dig +short api.redwood.team
getent hosts api.redwood.team
curl -v https://api.redwood.team/health
traceroute -n $(dig +short api.redwood.team | head -n1)
# aws checks
aws route53 list-hosted-zones-by-vpc --vpc-id vpc-central
aws route53resolver list-resolver-rule-associations --filters Name=VPC,Values=vpc-central
aws ec2 describe-vpc-endpoints --vpc-endpoint-ids vpce-0c9f
```

tim_customer: After PHZ association + SG change, dig returns private ENI IP, curl TLS handshake succeeds, and errors dropped to zero. We did see one 502 spike during a rolling deploy when an AZ's ENI health briefly transitioned.

alice_support: That's expected — TTL refresh combined with an AZ ENI being unhealthy can cause a small burst of failed requests. Lower TTLs during cutovers or stagger AZ deployments to reduce impact. Also verify endpoint ENI health and target group health.

raj_engineer: We'll add a KB entry: "TGW + central resolver + PrivateLink: PHZ association and forwarding rules checklist" — includes the commands above, SG/NACL guidance, and TTL/deploy notes.

deploybot: ticket created RW-7420 (KB + infra follow-up)

tim_customer: Thanks all — association + SG changes fixed it. We'll follow up if anything else shows. :thumbsup:
